newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Zeitler opposes FX target for Euro Central Bank.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler opposes FX target for Euro Central Bank.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler on Wednesday recommended that the European Central Bank target a money supply rather than exchange rate goal as the basis for its monetary strategy.

"Gearing monetary policy to the euro's exchange rate against other currencies is ... not a viable option," Zeitler, who is also president of the state central bank in Bavaria, told the European Finance Convention in Dublin.
He said the euro curency must itself be a "stability anchor" for other currencies. In addition, the euro must take over the German mark's role as an international investment and reserve currency.
Zeitler said the European Central Bank, to gain public trust, must have as a precondition the ability to influence the "target variable sufficiently well with its instruments".
"These requirements are largely met by a monetary policy strategy which seeks to achieve price stability by using the money stock as an intermediate target," Zeitler said.
He said many studies had confirmed there was a longer-term link between the pace of monetary growth and the rate of inflation.

He said the Bundesbank, over the medium term, through its policy of monetary targeting had been able to keep the expansion of the money stock on a course which had been compatible with largely inflation-free growth.

Zeitler recommended that a European Central Bank make its monetary policy course transparent to the general public by setting a target for the growth of the money stock and consider supplementing such a target with some kind of inflation benchmark, especially at the start of monetary union.
"During the launch phase there will be a degree of uncertainty about the level at which a 'pan-European money stock' will settle," he said.
"A combination of "monetary target plus inflation outlook' could provide the central bank with extra transparency and credibility," Zeitler said.
He added, however, that he would advise against replacing monetary targeting by a price target.
"To put it bluntly, the central bank can influence the price level only indirectly, but it can influence the money stock directly," Zeitler said.
Zeitler warned that the European Central Bank can only be successful and can only use its instruments meaningfully if the member states are homogenous in fiscal policy terms.

"If the budget deficits rise steeply in one part of the monetary union, with consequences for the money stock and prices, the necessary increases in interest rates will affect all countries equally," he said.

For this reason he said monetary union needed an effective Stability Pact. He said the Pact required a quasi-automatic set of rules with effective self-committment to initiate the excessive deficit procedure and to impose sanctions.
